## Automated Status Summary
#### Scope
`research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/` is prepared to be handed to colleagues in the owner's work environment, and the rest of `research-program/` is published to a public repository. Two disclosure-class defects have already reached this tree, both invisible on a casual read:

- A credential scan printed token prefixes into a working file before it was caught by hand.
- A batch of issue bodies carried a drafting agent's private working-directory paths (`[LOCAL_WORKSPACE]/<Repo>/...`), which made twenty-two issues unactionable across the fleet and had to be repaired one by one.

Both were found by a person looking. Neither would have been caught by any check in this repository, because there is none. The bundle's own redaction pass is a one-time human-reviewed step, not a gate, so nothing prevents the next artifact from reintroducing what the last one removed.

Evidence: `research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/REDACTIONS.md` records the manual redaction pass and its scope reduction; `README.md` states the disclosure standard this issue enforces; `research-program/CHECKPOINT.md` records the repair of the path-citation defect.

#### Tasks
- [x] Add `scripts/check_publication_safety.py` scanning every file under `research-program/` for: an absolute home path (`[LOCAL_HOME]/`), a credential prefix (`[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`), a private-key header (`[PRIVATE_KEY_HEADER]`, `[PRIVATE_KEY_HEADER]`), a scratchpad or drafting-agent path (`[LOCAL_WORKSPACE]/`, `[LOCAL_WORKSPACE]/`, `[LOCAL_WORKSPACE]/`), and an internal hostname pattern (`[LOCAL_HOST]` or a bare `localhost:` port reference).
- [x] Report every hit in one pass with file, line number and which rule matched; do not stop at the first.
- [x] Support an explicit allowlist file, `research-program/.publication-allow`, holding one `path:rule` pair per line with a required trailing comment giving the reason, so a deliberate exception is visible and justified rather than a silent skip.
- [x] Exit non-zero on any unallowed hit; print a summary line naming the counts for every rule including the zeros, so a clean run is distinguishable from a run that scanned nothing.
- [x] Print the number of files scanned, so a guard that matched nothing because it walked the wrong directory is visible.
- [x] Add `.github/workflows/publication-guard.yml` running the script on pull requests and on pushes to the default branch.
- [x] Add `tests/test_publication_safety.py` with fixtures for each rule, an allowlisted exception, and a clean tree.

#### Acceptance criteria
- [x] `python scripts/check_publication_safety.py` exits non-zero on a fixture containing a token prefix and names the file, the line and the rule.
- [x] The same fixture allowlisted with a reason exits zero, and an allowlist entry without a reason is itself an error.
- [x] A clean tree exits zero and prints the per-rule counts including zeros and the number of files scanned.
- [x] Pointing the scanner at an empty directory fails rather than passing, because zero files scanned is not evidence of safety.
- [x] The workflow runs on pull requests and blocks merge on failure.

<!-- auto-status-summary:end -->
